newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST-HK NEWSPAPER HEADLINES - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK NEWSPAPER HEADLINES - AUG 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The performance of mainland Chinese immigrant students in this year's Hong Kong school exams was outstanding, and was comparable to that of top local schools.
-- SING TAO -- Macau casino boss Stanley Ho said a six-month gang war was over and tourism would start to recover this month.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa visited residents in public housing estates and said that his first priority was to resolve housing problems.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Shanghai teenagers are having extravagant summer holidays with pocket money ranging from HK$3,000 to $7,000 for the vacation. The more affluent life had made them more dependent and materialistic.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Rumours that Chinese companies would boost stakes in Cathay Pacific pushed the aviation share price high, despite its poor profit results. But both China National Aviation Corp and Citic Pacific denied intending to adjust their percentage of stake in Cathay.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The government is considering ending Hong Kong's status as a port of first asylum for Vietnamese boat people, leader Tung Chee-hwa said.

-- Beijing was introducing a reserve labour system to reduce the pressure on the government to provide jobs for high school leavers as widespread redundancies were expected to follow an overhaul of the state sector.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Beijing said there was no turning back from economic reform experiments. A senior official said conditions were ripe to establish a welfare safety net to guarantee adequate living standards for city dwellers.
